sections.h2: Which offices handle Boyd County property tax
sections.html:
Three offices share the job. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets values. The Sheriff's Office bills and collects the current year. The County Clerk picks up older delinquent bills.

The PVA values all real and personal property in the county, except items the Kentucky Department of Revenue assigns itself, such as public service companies, bank shares and vehicles. Mail for the PVA goes to PO Box 434, Catlettsburg, KY 41129. For a house, the PVA's number is where everything else on your bill begins.

sections.h2: Boyd County housing and tax base
sections.html:
Boyd County covers about 160 square miles with roughly 300 residents per square mile. The 2025 population estimate is 47,751 in about 21,818 housing units. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $130,700, the typical household earns $61,118, and owners live in 70.2% of homes. Owner costs run $1,217 a month with a mortgage and $463 without one.

A house near that value carries a smaller assessment than most Bluegrass homes, but the 911 fee and city levies still show up on the bill.

  • Ashland and Catlettsburg bill their own city property tax, so call the city, not the county, with questions about it.
  • The county bill carries a 911 service fee, and Boyd County 911 at 606-329-2191 answers questions about it.

The Sheriff's Office follows the calendar in KRS 134.015. Paying early earns a discount, the middle stretch is flat, and two penalty steps come after.

Payment schedule applied by the Boyd County Sheriff
When you payDiscount or penalty
By November 12% discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount, no penalty
January 1 to January 315% penalty
After January 3110% penalty

You can view and pay your bill online through the Sheriff's Office. The dates printed on a bill can run later than the statute's calendar when the state allows an alternative collection schedule, so read your bill and ask the sheriff's office which dates apply to your parcel. When the sheriff's collection period ends, unpaid prior year taxes move to the County Clerk at 606-739-5116, option 4.

sections.h2: How to contest a Boyd County assessment
sections.html:
Start with the PVA. Value is fixed as of January 1, and whenever a property's value goes up from the year before, the PVA mails the owner a notice of change. That notice is your cue to look at the number closely, since the conference window is short.

Your first step is a conference with the PVA or a deputy. The window is six days a week for two weeks, starting the first Monday in May, though dates can shift. If you leave without agreement, a written petition to the County Clerk earns you a hearing before the board of assessment appeals, as KRS 133.120 provides.

  • Bring comparable sales, an appraisal, photos of damage or a contractor's repair estimate.
  • Ask to hold the conference by phone if a visit is hard.
  • The petition must state your reasons and your opinion of the property's fair cash value.
  • Keep paying while you appeal, since an appeal does not hold up the tax.

sections.h2: Does Boyd County have a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, the statewide one, for owners who reach 65 or are classed as totally disabled. For the two years covering 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100.

File with the Boyd County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves your age. A disability claim needs proof of a total-disability classification from a federal or retirement program, and it is refiled yearly unless the owner has a service-connected disability or has been found permanently disabled.

For an owner on a fixed income, the exemption and an on-time payment in the discount window can matter more than a small change in value. Before listing, ask the PVA whether an exemption application is on file.

sections.h2: Key dates in the assessment year
sections.html:
• January 1: the assessment date for every property.
  • First Monday in May: the roll inspection period normally opens and PVA conferences begin.
  • Third Monday in May: the inspection period normally ends, and the written petition follows within a workday.
  • November 1: the last day for the 2% discount.
  • December 31: the last day to pay the plain face amount.
  • January 31: the last day before the 10% penalty.

A notice on the county's tax page announces when each year's collection begins. The dates printed on your own bill win, since the state can set an alternative schedule.

sections.h2: Who can speak for me in an appeal?
sections.html:
You can appear yourself or send an agent. Kentucky law limits who may be paid to represent an owner at a PVA conference or a board hearing.

  • An attorney or a certified public accountant.
  • A tax consultant, or a real estate broker or sales associate who holds a Kentucky license.
  • An employee of the property owner.
  • A real property appraiser who holds a Kentucky license or certification.

An agent needs your written authorization and must disclose any personal stake, such as a contingency fee. Losing at the county board leaves one more stop, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, and only owners who went to the county board first may use it.

The statute's calendar makes the cost easy to see in percentages. Pay by November 1 and you get 2% off. Pay from November 2 through December 31 and you owe the face amount. January adds a 5% penalty, and after January 31 the statutory penalty is 10%. Extra charges can attach once a bill moves to the clerk, so get a payoff figure from that office before closing.

Your own bill carries county, school and district amounts plus the 911 fee, and the Sheriff's Office can give you the exact total for your parcel.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller before listing
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps the tax side of a sale from surprising you.

  1. Find your latest bill and check which dates apply to your parcel.
  2. Ask the Sheriff's Office whether this year is paid in full.
  3. Call the County Clerk at 606-739-5116, option 4, if any earlier year is still open.
  4. Phone the city if you live in Ashland or Catlettsburg and ask whether a city bill is outstanding.
  5. Ask the PVA whether your value changed and whether a homestead exemption is on file.
  6. Hand your closing agent the payoff figures so nothing is found late.

Doing this before the first showing means no tax question is left to hold up the contract.

sections.h2: Selling a Boyd County house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Delinquent tax attaches to the house as a lien, and the debt itself belongs to the owner as of the assessment date. A title company will want any unpaid bill cleared at closing.

  • This year's bill unpaid: the Sheriff's Office gives the exact amount.
  • An older year unpaid: the County Clerk's office quotes it.
  • City tax questions: City of Ashland, 606-385-3275, or City of Catlettsburg, 606-739-5223.
  • Escrow: ask the lender whether it has already paid.

If you cannot pay beforehand, ask the closing agent to deduct it from your sale proceeds. A cash buyer or an ordinary buyer both expect the same thing: a bill that is paid or a payoff figure the title company can read.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Boyd County?
faqs.a: The Boyd County Sheriff's Office collects the current year's tax. The County Clerk collects delinquent taxes from prior years.

faqs.q: What is the Boyd County property tax discount?
faqs.a: KRS 134.015 allows 2% off for payment in full by November 1, then the plain amount until December 31. The dates printed on your bill control.

faqs.q: How do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the Boyd County Clerk's office at 606-739-5116 and press option 4, or use the clerk's website.

faqs.q: When can I meet with the Boyd County PVA about my assessment?
faqs.a: Before the roll inspection window ends. It normally opens the first Monday in May and closes the third Monday.

faqs.q: Do Ashland and Catlettsburg charge their own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Questions about city property tax go to the City of Ashland at 606-385-3275 or the City of Catlettsburg at 606-739-5223.
